chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about eating the tortoise, so he said, 'Indeed, the tortoise, the mouse, the monkey, and the pigs are musakh (transformed species).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating tortoise in Shia fiqh according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) classifies the tortoise, along with the mouse, monkey, and pig, as *musakh* (transformed species), thereby rendering their consumption impermissible. This ruling draws upon the Quranic narrative of the Banu Israel, where specific groups were transformed into animals as divine punishment, establishing a theological basis for their distinct biological and legal status in Shia jurisprudence. The inclusion of the tortoise in this list highlights the scholarly tradition of linking zoological characteristics with metaphysical origins to determine dietary laws.
